The experimental analysis of the proposed approach is done on the dataset where the videos are captured using the camera as well as from the other resources such as Internet. Noisy videos are prepared by mixing the Salt & Pepper noise with different noise densities (levels) in the video dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms the traditional approaches not only in terms of noise reduction but also in preserving the details in the video.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Different Windowing Based LP FIR Filters in Synchronization of Discrete-Time Chaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The wideband nature of chaotic signals makes synchronization difficult when the communication channel imposes bandwidth constraints. Here, an allied communication system and a discrete-time master-slave system that synchronizes despite channel bandwidth are considered. Also, the effect of types of windows used for the design of linear-phase Low Pass (LP) Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter in the synchronization of discrete-time chaotic systems under bandlimited channels is depicted. The synchronization is accomplished by using a digital filter to restrict the spectral content of the feedback loop that generates the transmitted signal. The three-dimensional generalization of the Wang system map [17] is considered for the study of discrete-time chaotic systems with the help of numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Optimal Siting and Sizing Approach of Plug-in Electric Vehicle Fast Charging Station using a Novel Meta-heuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: As climate change becomes a significant concern, fostering the use of electric vehicles (EVs) has emerged as an effective remedy to the pollution caused by fossil-fuel transportation. Placing charging stations with growing charging infras-tructure is significant to EVs' accessibility and future viability. The location of fast-charging stations (FCSs) and their size are critical for the distribution network. Therefore, this paper focuses on FCS's optimal placement and size in the distribution network. Moreover, the energy loss cost for the distribution network and transportation loss cost from the demand point to FCSs for charging the battery is considered decision functions to optimize the location and size of FCSs. In addition, integrating PV distributed generations (PVGs) is also urged for the optimal location and size of FCSs to reduce the grid dependency due to the additional demand for charging. A meta-heuristic opti-mization approach is proposed for the optimal solution to locate the FCS with size. Furthermore, the IEEE-34 bus distribution system with PVDGs integration is suggested to implement the proposed optimization problem. For this work, the direct load flow technique is employed to analyze the load flow of the proposed IEEE 34 distribution system. The presented distribution system's active power flow and bus voltages are investigated for two recommended cases.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control of Multi-Area Power System using Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA)
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Load Frequency Control (LFC) is the key to the proper functioning of the power system. Thus, it has been and persists to be an important area of research and would continue to be so with the ever-growing needs and complexity of the power system. Numerous techniques have been developed and proposed to achieve load frequency control. This paper discusses one of the most efficient methods known for the optimization of the LFC problem, i.e the Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA). The algorithm discussed is applicable to both single as well as multi-area systems. The results are analysed given the effectiveness to achieve LFC and the robustness of the system.

articleTitle: Load Flow Analysis of HVAC HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The paper presents load flow analysis of 30 bus HVAC system using Newton Raphson Technique. In this 30 bus HVAC system, an HVDC link is incorporated between bus 9 and bus 28, thus making HVAC HVDC system. The load flow analysis of this HVAC HVDC system is performed by sequential solution technique which converts the HVDC link into equivalent active and reactive power injections by making use of combination 1 of specified control parameters. Further net power injections are calculated at these buses, thus making the entire system as pure AC system whose load flow analysis is then performed by Newton Rapshon method.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of High performance of a BLDC Motor for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Brushless DC motors are widely used in electric vehicle due to its prominent features. It's torque to weight ratio is made high. The approach of developing a BLDC motor is described in this work, along with comprehensive design equations. Motor geometry is created using ANSYS by RMxprt tool. For further investigation, the analytical design is subsequently implemented in Maxwell 2D. The brushless DC design motor has obtained an efficiency of 87.2% that is very important for electric vehicle perspective.

articleTitle: PV Array Dynamic Reconfiguration by leveling the Solar Irradiance under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Solar photovoitaic (PV) energy generation system is the major part of renewable energy that can full-fill the growing demands and reduction in conventional energy at negligible op-erating cost with nil greenhouse gas emission. However, efficiency of Solar PV needs to be enhanced, and it can be achieved by PV array reconfiguration along with maximum power point tracking (MPPT). However, the reconfiguration based on physical relocation of the modules is time consuming and limited to known shading patterns and small PV energy generation systems. Therefore, PV Array Dynamic Reconfiguration by leveling the solar irradiance is proposed in this paper. After reconfiguration, the global maximum power point is tracked by the P and O optimization technique. The main advantage of the proposed technique is the reduction of the number of switches applied for the reconfiguration under partial shading conditions.

articleTitle: Improved Electric spring control for Power Factor Correction Using Fuzzy PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper Electric spring has been used as Reactive power compensator for Demand Side Management (DSM) in order to mitigate adverse effects of discontinuity in electric power generated by Renewable Energy Sources. Electric spring has multitude of advantages like providing voltage stability, improving power quality and diminution of power imbal-ance. A new generation of Load is being used for improving power factor by use of Hybrid algorithms consisting Proportional Integral (PI) and Fuzzy logic controllers (FLC). Results from the MATLAB/Simulink software illustrates that an electric spring regulates line voltage regardless of changes in load thereby resulting in improved power factor.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal DG Allocation using Centrality Index and ABC Optimization for Three-phase UDS
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Main priority of the distribution system is to provide reliable and good quality power supply to the consumers by regulating the voltage profile and voltage unbalanced factor of the unbalanced distribution system (UDS). This paper presents a multi-objective optimization method for multi-point allocation of DGs for three-phase UDS to reduce the sum of active power loss (SAPL) and improve voltage profile and unbalanced factor of UDS. For improvement and maintenance of voltage profile in UDS, the choice of DG location is very crucial to improve the overall performance parameters of UDS. A graph-theoretic approach called “electrical centrality Index” is used to find out the site of DGs. Once the location of the DG is decided, the size of the DG is optimized by applying an artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm. The proposed method requires single-stage optimization unlike the two-stage optimization required for optimal DG placement in most of the existing methods; which makes the suggested method faster and simpler in implementation. The proposed approach is tested for 25 bus UDS to determine its efficacy.

articleTitle: An Efficient Key Agreement Protocol for Smart Grid communication
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Integration of technology with power grid emerged Smart grid. The advancement of power grid into smart grid faces some security issues like message mod-ification attacks, message injection attacks etc. If these issues are correctly not addressed, then the performance of the smart grid is degraded. Smart grid has bidirectional communication among the smart grid entities. The flow of user energy consumption information between all smart grid entities may lead the user privacy violation. Smart grids have various components but service providers and smart meters are the main components. Smart meters have sensing and communication functionality, while service providers have control and communication functionality. There are many privacy preservation schemes proposed that ensure the cus-tomer's privacy in the smart grid. To preserve the customer's data privacy and communication, authentication and key agreement schemes are required between the smart meter and the service provider. This paper proposes an efficient key agreement protocol to handle several security challenges in smart grid. The proposed protocol is tested against the various security attributes necessary for a key establishment protocol and found safe. Further the performance of the proposed work is compared with several others existing work for smart grid application and it has been observed that the proposed protocol performs significantly better than the existing protocols available in the literature.

articleTitle: Optical Tracking System for Auto-Registration of Multiple Views of a 3D Scanner for 3D Shape Reconstruction of Components
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for optically tracking a 3D scanner for auto-registration of multiple views of the 3D scanner. This method involves calibration of the system, capturing the scanner images, marker detection, 2D correspondence, 3D correspondence and then computing the required transformation for registration of the captured views. The optical tracker described in this paper is stereo vision based system. 3D scanner used in the experiment is the digital fringe projection based 3D Scanner fitted with IR based retro-reflective markers.

articleTitle: Impact of Distinct Weather Parameters on Simultaneous Prediction of Solar Power and Load Demand using LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Forecasting of solar energy and load demand plays very vital role in energy management system. Forecasting of load and solar power depend on various factors like time horizon, weather conditions etc. of region. So to have their accurate prediction, it is necessary to consider as many factors as possible that affect the uncertainties of solar generation and load demand. This paper has considered different weather parameters like air density, radiance, temperature, precipitation, cloud cover and irradiance to predict solar based power generation and load demand simultaneously using long short term memory (LSTM) models. The root mean square error and mean absolute percentage error metrics are used to analyze the performance of the above framed structure.

articleTitle: Performance and Energy Metrics Analysis of Stand Alone Rooftop PV plant
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Due to the easy installation, low operating costs, and financial assistance from the Indian government, rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems have become a popular alternative electricity source for domestic users. The time to time, detailed studies of such systems are required to improve their energy efficiency. In this paper, performance and energy metrics analysis of a 5.76 kWp Stand Alone Rooftop Photovoltaic (SARP) system is done for the climatic conditions of Kajra (Bihar), India. The SARP system is supplying electrical energy to the domestic load of 4.3 kW, for which the average daily electricity consumption is 21.11 kWh. With two 150 Ah battery bank as a backup source, the PVsyst based performance analysis shows that the SARP system has final yield, capacity utilisation factor (CUF), and performance ratio (PR) of 3.28, 13.65% and 71.3% respectively. The energy metrics analysis shows that the system has energy pay-back time (EPBT) of 5.74 years and electricity production factor (EPF) value of 4.34 (on life time basis). The analysis of performance and energy metrics reveals that the SARP systems are efficient systems for rural location-based household electricity use.

articleTitle: Denoising of Images using Fractional Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, we are using fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) for the application of image processing. Our objective is to use the FrFT in such a way that it can provide the solution to image denoising issues on a larger scale. The assertion behind using FrFT is that it has been broadly used and validated in the context of signal processing as a time-frequency analytical tool. Many used cases are available in the context of signal processing, such as detection, filtering, and feature extraction of the signal. Considering these studies, we use the FrFT to enhance and denoise the images using a parallel set of filters. Through simulation, we have observed that our method has outstanding and comparable outcomes in terms of accuracy concerning the existing denoising algorithms.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Different Meta-heuristic Optimization Based Tuning of PI Controllers for Vector Controlled Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this research study, different meta-heuristic optimization techniques are used for tuning of PI controller used in vector-controlled Induction Motor (IM) Drive. This drive involves two current controllers for the inner current control loop for controlling direct axis and quadrature axis currents. One PI controller is in the outer loop for controlling the rotor speed. For the better and stable performance of the drive, proper tuning of these three PI controllers is mandatory. Therefore, to solve this problem, some tuning rules are necessary to be applied. From this consideration, six different meta-heuristic optimization methods are implemented to the vector-controlled IM drive and comparative analysis based on the dynamics performance of the drive is presented. The results are verified on MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

articleTitle: Optimal Emplacement and Allocation of Distributed Generators by Using Ant Lion Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Renewable energy sources, used as a sort of Distribution Generations (DGs) technology in Radial Distribution Networks (RDN), improve both electrical energy generation and RDN performance. In this article, the Ant Lion optimizing (ALO) algorithm was used to find the best DG allocation and sizing in a balanced RDN for minimizing total operating cost, power loss and voltage deviation index that improves voltage stability index and voltage profile. Candidate buses for DG installation are identified using the loss sensitivity factor (LSF), while a suitable bus location is selected using the voltage sensitivity factor (VSF). In this study, IEEE 33 bus test system has been used at various load levels under constant power load. To test this technique's superiority and performance, the proposed method's numerical results has been compared with other optimization approaches.

articleTitle: Design of Compact Dual Band Microstrip Antenna using DGS and Shorting Post Methods
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper a low profile, compact dual band microstrip antenna has been presented. The proposed design for the size reduction consists of hybrid techniques that is both Shorting Post and Defected Ground Structure (DGS). DGS is produced by trimming circular slots on the ground and Shorting posts are drilled as Plated through Holes (PTH) through the substrate from patch to ground for more reduction of the size. Implementing these results in increase of antenna electrical length which accompanied with raise in the path of current distribution. The final designed antenna is compared with conventional patch antenna which is designed without size reduction methods. The resulting final antenna is smaller than the conventional patch antenna by 42.25%. The designed antenna is fabricated and it's characteristics are tested using Vector Network Analyser and proposed design resonates at both 900 MHz and 1800 MHz frequencies which we use for Global System for Mobile(GSM) applications. This antenna is used in many wireless communication systems like Laptop, Cell Phone, Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR) where compactness is required.

articleTitle: Identification of Faulty IGBT in Vector Controlled PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM) have become more popular for industrial applications due to their unique advantage of high power density and efficiency. The reliability and safety of PMSM is an essential requirement for smooth operation. An open-circuit fault in the inverter affects the PMSM drive's performance, causing excessive speed and torque fluctuations. This paper proposed an Integral Current Error (ICE) technique for identifying faulty IGBT by analyzing the performance of the PMSM drive. The proposed technique is implemented in MATLAB/SIMULINK platform. Simulation results and outcomes the fault identification are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: An Improved Arduino Based Automatic Transfer Switching System For PV System As Well As Standby Electric Generator
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The utilization of clean and renewable energy in daily life is a difficult task due to power supply interruptions, and the biggest issue is transferring that energy from one location to another at a low cost. To make the system more reliable, we propose a new technique for transmitting energy from one location to another without interruption, as well as a trustworthy and reliable islanding system that we can use in our industries and at home. We are currently dealing with pollution and a scarcity of nonrenewable resources such as coal. As a result, there may be power outages. As the number of power outages rises, so does the amount of money lost in various industrial and commercial sectors. As for that problem, the suggested solution is to utilize many energy sources (both renewable and non-renewable), and if one of the energy sources is unavailable, we must switch to another. However, there are two sorts of switching operations: manual switching and automatic switching. There are issues with manual switchings, such as power loss, time wasted, and short circuits. We'll use automatic transfer switching to swap between these sources for that reason. We mostly use renewable energy sources, and switching to renewable energy sources is beneficial for improving power quality. We employ electricity from solar cells, public power supplies (such as MSEB), and generators to analyze and test the system's compatibility. We may use various renewable energy sources in our system, and we only employ non-renewable energy sources in an emergency.

articleTitle: Analysis and Performance Evolution of Novel Global Modified Flower Pollination Algorithm for Photovoltaic System under Partial Shading Condition
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Maximum Power Point (MXPP) tracking controller is used in solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to maximize output under varying atmospheric conditions. The appearance of several peaks owing to partial shade and complicate the tracking procedure. Despite the widespread usage of conventional and soft computing approaches to handle MXPP tracking problems, due of the set step size of conventional methods, their performance is restricted, whereas Soft computing approaches, on the other hand, are limited by a lack of randomness once they reach a certain point of maximum power. As a result, a Modified Flower Pollination Algorithm (MFPA) is suggested in this study, which has the capacity to attain a global peak. The MFP A method's optimization process combines global and local searching in a single step, and it's a crucial component of the MXPP tracking application's success. The algorithm's robustness is tested using a uniform and partial shading patterns. Furthermore, the MFP A technique is subjected to a full performance evaluation via simulation, which is quantified using standard PSO methodologies. Furthermore, the MFP A technique is subjected to a full performance evaluation via simulation, which is quantified using standard PSO methodologies.

articleTitle: Butterfly Optimization Algorithm for PV Array Reconfiguration to Achieve Higher GMP during PSCs
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Uneven irradiation, such as partial shadowing, can have a bad effect on SPV system efficiency (PSCs). Using power-voltage (P-V) characteristics, describe a characterization approach for investigating numerous power peaks, such as the global maximum power point (GMPP) and local maximum power point (LMPP). In order to reduce the shading effect, a reshuffling method of PV modules is used in an array system, which improves shade dispersion throughout the entire PV array. There are distinct ways based on game theory accessible, however, due to the high wire length requirements, optimization techniques are becoming more prevalent. When compared to standard PV arrangements such as series-parallel (SP) and total-cross, the butterfly optimization (BO) technique displays effective shade dispersion for all shading circumstances. Using shading scenarios, the proposed concept is evaluated in terms of power and voltage at GMPP, PL, and FF levels. MATLAB/Simulink is used exclusively for this investigation.

articleTitle: Hybrid EVs Using SWOT Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The electric vehicles charging infrastructure (EVsCI) has transformed the automobile industry. The globe will switch to renewable electric vehicles in the near future. In today's global economy, solar and wind power, as well as other renewable energy sources, are becoming more important. In addition to the Electric Vehicles (EVs) policies, this article discusses the EVs scenario in India. The SWOT Analysis, which includes Strengths (S), Weaknesses (W), Opportunities (O), and Threats (T) variables, is used to identify and define the barriers for EVs & EVsCI. This analysis also helps in identifying and defining the drivers for EVs industry and its charging infrastructure. This analysis may help overall growth and development of this industry on a worldwide scale. SWOT analysis is used in this research to establish hybrid EVs, its EVsCI and develop a hybrid EVs framework that includes battery, & solar energy to manufacture right & suitable Hybrid EVs by the industries and provide proper EVsCI.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Based Image Edge Detection Using Improved Cuckoo Search Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are designed to find the best solution by removing the solutions with the lowest fitness. As a result, this research provides an evolutionary algorithm-based edge detection approach. The best filter coefficients and thresholding procedure are obtained using a training dataset consisting of simple pictures and their related optimal edge characteristics. The Cuckoo Search optimization algorithm is an effective mechanism inspired by the brood behavior of cuckoo birds. In this research work, an enhanced cuckoo search algorithm is proposed which improvises the search capability of identifying multi-threshold values for edge detection. An efficient Fuzzy Logic technique is also applied to segment the image based on fuzzy membership functions. The proposed model evaluation shows the significance in different images.

articleTitle: Dielectric Performance of ZnO and CuO-based Synthetic Ester Fluid under Temperature Variation
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Nanotechnology offers an advanced method to improve the dielectric characteristics of insulating oil used in transformers. The increase in power demand calls for an increase in power transmission and requires such an insulant that offers better dielectrics and cooling properties in the form of synthetic esters. In this study, conducting (ZnO) and semiconducting (CuO) nanoparticles are used in three different concentrations (0.01 wt%, 0.02 wt%, and 0.03 wt%) to prepare Synthetic ester-based nanofluids. The dielectric properties such as AC breakdown voltage, Dielectric Dissipation factor, and DC resistivity are investigated for the pure synthetic ester oil and its corresponding NF for the temperature range 23 °C – 60 °C at an interval of 20 °C. The breakdown test is performed according to IEC-60247 experimental standards. The instrument containing the Dissipation Factor Bridge, resistivity meter, and heating oil cell is used to determine the Dissipation factor and resistivity of oil. The results show that ZnO nanofluid (NF) exhibits higher breakdown voltage than CuO-NF except at 0.02 wt%, furthermore, the lowest dissipation factor is shown by CuO-NF even at elevated temperature.

articleTitle: PID and Backstepping Controller on a 2-Link Biped Robot
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper deals with the application of PID controller and backstepping controller to the 2-link biped robot considering the non-linearities, parameter uncertainties, unmodelled dynamics related to it like parameter disturbance, unknown joint friction, inertia, different payloads and external perturbations). The trajectory tracking of a 2-link biped robot utilizing these two controllers is presented in this paper. The fundamental purpose of research is to identify the robustness of controller for trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Identification of Power Transformer Insulation Condition Sensitive Parameters using Initial Slope of RVM
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Power transformers are one of the critical components of the Power System. Insulation failure is the major cause of transformer breakdown. Hence, proper insulation diagnosis is important for the reliable operation of a power system. Most of the available methods for the assessment of transformer insulation condition involves the use of costly equipment. In this work, a technique for estimating power transformer insulation condition sensitive parameters has been proposed that utilizes the Return Voltage Measurement (RVM) data measured using low-cost equipment. RVM is a known technique for the condition assessment of power transformer insulation. Here, a method is proposed to estimate insulation resistance, paper moisture and zero of the transfer function using the initial slope of the RVM spectra.

articleTitle: RT-HIL Implementation of Synchrophasor Phase Angle Unwrapping using ROC Method
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: With the growth in the transmission and distribution infrastructure, there has been a rising need for monitoring various parameters of the system in real-time. Phasor measurement units (PMUs) are capable of providing time-synchronized values of bus voltages and currents, which can further be utilized for visualization purposes. The phase angles computed by PMUs are wrapped around +/− 180 degrees, and proper unwrapping techniques must be incorporated in the phasor data concentrators (PDCs) to obtain accurate values of angle differences of two PMUs which are located at different locations. This paper focuses on the unwrapping of phase angles that are obtained from PMUs placed in a real-time hardware in the loop (RT-HIL) environment, by using the rollover counter (ROC) method. The OSIsoft PI system is used as a PDC for collecting the synchrophasor data and performing the various calculations on the phase angles obtained from the PMUs. The PI system does not have any unwrapping techniques and hence the ROC method was incorporated in this paper to successfully unwrap the phase angles.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filtering Process for Two-Dimensional Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, a novel adaptive approach of Cubature Kalman filter (CKF) is implemented for two-dimensional target tracking problem. This novel approach uses residual-innovation approach for adjusting the noise covariances for process. The measurement noise covariance is adjusted based on the covariance matching method. The novelty exists with the formulation of adaptation law for process and measurement noise covariances. The effectiveness of proposed algorithm is compared with traditional CKF, UKF and EKF by calculating root mean square error (RMSE) of states in 500 Monte Carlo runs. The relative computational time, mean and standard deviation of RMSEs for considered filtering techniques are also presented. The simulation results show improvement in estimation performance with adaptive CKF (ACKF) approach than others for target tracking system dealing with Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise distributions.

articleTitle: A Local Feature Extraction Mechanism for Effective Content Based Image Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A CBIR system works on the primitive visual features extracted from the images of a concerned database. A CBIR system should provide better results and need to have a close resemblance with human perception. So, to keep these points in mind, in this paper, we have proposed a CBIR system that works on local image features to provide better efficiency. In contrast, the HSV color model has been incorporated as it is closest to human perception. Various statistical parameters are evaluated from H and S components for the color features extraction. Now, for texture and shape features BDIP and BVLC are deployed. This work has been validated through various benchmark databases, and overlying results are capable enough to demonstrate its superiority over contemporaries.

articleTitle: Enhanced Dynamic Characteristics Of Bidirectional DC-DC SEPIC/ZETA Converter Based BESS
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In the current scenario, much research is being done on renewable energy generation, electric vehicles, etc. In such systems, a battery energy storage system (BESS) is utilized to make functioning more reliable. For voltage management of a dc bus, this paper suggests a charging/discharging system using a BESS. In this paper, a bidirectional dc-dc SEPIC/ZETA converter with PID (proportional-integral-derivative) controller is demonstrated. The converter's state-space circuit averaged modelling-based transfer function approach is presented to control the switching pulses of the converter for SEPIC and ZETA modes. The controller tuning is presented by the classical Ziegler-Nichols method and PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization) tool. The operation of the system with bidirectional power flow control has been simulated and verified through MATLAB/SIMULINK results in both charging and discharging states of the battery under varying circumstances.

articleTitle: Development of an oil film-coated QCM sensor for detection of ß-myrcene in black pepper
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Black pepper is called the “King of spices” worldwide for its spice and medicinal value. It is one of the essential commercial spices for India. Black paper quality identification and classification depend based on the presence of VOCs. p-myrcene is one of the VOCs by which the different cultivars of black pepper can be classified. A jojoba oil-coated QCM sensor (JOJ-QCM) has been fabricated. The sensor shows a sensitivity of 0.1218 Hz/ppm for the detection of p-myrcene. Moreover, different sensor characteristics like sensitivity, selectivity, repeatability, and humidity were studied to validate the sensor performance.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Triboelectric Nanogenerators For Energy Harvesting Applications and Development of Data Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Scavenging energy from wasted or unused power has been an interesting topic among the researchers for a long time. With prodigious growth in mobile and portable electronics, IoT, big data, artificial intelligence, health monitoring system it becomes necessary to develop energy storage technology to make these systems self-powered. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG) which works on the basis of the combined effect of triboelectrification, and electrostatic induction provides a possible solution for harvesting ambient mechanical energy that is abundant but wasted in our daily life. In this paper we have compared the peak output voltage of two different TENGs made up of cotton fiber paper-polymeric cellulose film, Polyimide (Kapton)s'- Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) when a low frequency hand tapping is applied to each of them. We have also presented a data acquisition (DAQ) scheme of the generated voltage and stored the collected output data as a waveform graph in LabVIEW 2018 software. These acquired data can be later used for further explorations like modeling of TENG devices using system identification technique.

articleTitle: Wind Energy Generation for Local Load with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The control technique for a wind energy generator with energy storage battery system (ESBS) in an islanded Grid is presented in this research. This Islanded Micro Grid (IM G) consists of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind energy conversion system, and battery storage. The suggested methodology includes a dc/dc bidirectional converter for charging/discharging the battery and consuming/providing the excess deficit power required by load to maintain the constant frequency at the PCC. A proportional-integral control method is employed in traditional battery control, which can create stability issues, therefore a control mechanism is discussed in this article. which improves the stability of the system and makes it easier to operate. The control algorithm's effectiveness under various dynamic and steady-state settings are observed. To improve the effectiveness of the system, the battery is used which, feed the loads when the wind speed is too low. The Load Side Voltage source Converter(LSVSC) is utilised in the islanded Micro Grid for voltage and frequency control. Local load reactive power and harmonic currents are compensated with this control. In wind energy generation system (WEGS), the perturb and observe method is utilised for maximum power point (MPP) tracking. Due to concerns with variation in generator speed and continual nonlinear loads, a backup battery is connected at the dc link of the LSVSC, utilising a bidirectional dc/dc converter for power balancing between the load and the source in an islanded microgrid. The control method has been validated by test results in MATLAB simulation, which shows that it can improve the system's power quality under varied wind speed and load variation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Battery Charging Circuits using Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper gives idea about the comprehensive study followed by comparative analysis of various maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques using different charging circuits for battery. The circuitry modeling has been done and implemented in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The peak power of photovoltaic (PV) array is tracked using three different algorithms, namely perturb and observe (P&O), fuzzy logic controller (FLC) and incremental conductance (IC) algorithms. Buck, Boost and Zeta topologies have been employed as a DC-DC converter for battery charging and battery charge controller implementation. A total of nine models have been developed and compared. Comparison of the model has been done with following performance parameters; battery rating, controller efficiency, steady state time, charging current, charging current ripple and charging voltage ripple. The performance and comparison results show which parameters are better in relevant model.

articleTitle: Investigation on Loss Allocation in Distribution Network with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The presence of distributed generations (DGs) in a distribution network (DN) affects network operation. It alters the network losses. The losses in DN lines may vary based on the placement of DGs in the network. One such impact is on the network participants' loss allocation. The allocation of losses among network participants is determined by its contribution to the losses. This paper investigates the distribution of losses to the network participants with the integration of DGs in DN. The investigation is carried out on 15-bus and 33-bus single-phase radial test DN. Pro-rata and Branch Current Decomposition(BCD) methods are used to allocate line losses. The variation in the loss allocation results in optimally and non-optimally placed DGs in DN are analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power High Gain Structure of Bulk Driven OTA
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, a non-conventional design is proposed to increase the gain by boosting the impedance at the output stage of a bulk-driven based OTA. The input is a bulk-driven stage configured in a flip voltage follower (FVF) mode for low-voltage operation. The output of the proposed amplifier uses QFG based self cascode stage since the gain of the amplifier is limited due to the low transconductance of bulk-driven input transistors. The QFG technique in self cascode helps in scaling the threshold voltage of the MOS transistor, which results in improved performance of self cascode, thereby increasing the amplifier gain. The achieved DC gain is 54.45dB with a unity gain bandwidth of 52.85MHz. The proposed circuit is designed and analyzed using Cadence software on the MOSFET models of UMC twin-well CMOS 0.18µm technology at a dual supply of 0.5volt.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic-based tuning and analysis of different algorithms of Fractional-order integral Differential (FOPID) controller for non-integer Order systems
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper consists of meta-heuristic-based tuning methods of Fractional order proportional integral differentiation (F.O.PID) controller for a non-integer-order system has been discussed and analyzed. The main objective is to get a solution a set of non-linear equations carrying inequalities unlike that of an integer-order proportional integral differential (I.O.PID) controller which only contains fewer parameters that need to be tuned. The main contents consist of designing, simulation, and the Model reduction of FOPID controllers for a non-integer-order system. Following the proposed schemes, the Fractional-order Proportion integral (F. O.PI) controller and F. O.PID controller perform effectively. Moreover, the design of FOPID using meta-heuristic algorithms clearly defeats the FOPI controller. To verify this fact and validate the proposed tuning schemes, simulation results are shown.

Author Keywords: Fractional order Proportional Integral Differentiation Controller

articleTitle: External parasitic loaded pin diode integrated multiband frequency reconfigurable antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A triangular patch frequency reconfigurable an-tenna is designed for wireless and UWB applications. Frequency reconfigurability is achieved by inserting PIN diodes between the radiating patch and the three parasitic stubs. The gained frequencies at 2.1 – 2.6 GHz and 2.7 – 7.3 GHz are propagated by incorporating patches around the radiating patch and placing the diodes in between the PIN patches. The multi-band operation is accomplished using the parasitic patches and PIN diodes. The designed antenna can strain the frequency from ultra-wideband to multi-band. Gain and Radiation Efficiency are improved in the perspective design. Along with the wireless applications, the designed antenna is covering the lower frequencies of C- band. Co and cross polarizations are refined in both E and H plane.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling and Performance Investigation of Six-Phase and Three-Phase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A d-q axis model of six-phase induction motor is developed and the performance investigation is done in this paper. The performance of traditional three-phase induction motor and six-phase induction motors is compared. Comparison is done on the basis of rotor speed, stator current and torque developed by three-phase and six-phase induction machines. The modelling equation has been described, and the machine's equivalent circuit has been created using the mathematical equations. The advantage of Six-phase induction motor is found as; without increasing phase voltage the value of current per phase is reduced, less harmonic distortion of stator current, Speed variation and slip is less in 6-phase IM. It is observed that six-phase machine requires less current to produce same electromagnetic torque, it also increases the power handling capability for same size as compared to three-phase machine.

articleTitle: A Novel way of Characterizing the Reverberation Chamber using CST
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The rising demand for wireless devices has resulted in a significant increase in the use of reverberation chambers (RCs). Reverberation chambers are utilized to assess sensitive emissions and carry out immunity tests at a lower cost. Even though the tests in an RC are faster than traditional anechoic chambers, the tests required to certify the RC itself often take several days. This paper presents a simpler and much faster way to characterize a reverberation chamber using an electromagnetic simulation software called CST Studio. Field Uniformity within the chamber has been evaluated and the results obtained were observed to be within the limits proposed by the standard IEC 61000–4 21.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Management in Multi-Area Network using Artificial Jellyfish search optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Multi-area economic dispatch (MAED) is an extension of economic dispatch and become much more complex to solve due to additional tie-line constraints associated with it. In this paper, a newly proposed jellyfish search (JS) algorithm is implemented for the solution to the MAED problem. Jellyfish found in the ocean, travel from one place to another in search of food sources with passive and active motion with a unique time control mechanism. The jellyfish search (JS) algorithm is a global optimizer; it includes the natural behavior of jellyfish in its Analytical modal for the solution of complex contained optimization problems. To validate the effectiveness of JS is tested on two complex constrained MAED problems. Comparison of simulation results of the tested problem are made with reported results by other metaheuristic supports to claim of its efficacy in searching for promising results and better-constrained handing capability.

articleTitle: DC Transient Current Polarity based Protection Scheme for Grid Connected PV System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Integration of the renewable energy sources to the existing power system changes the radial nature of the conventional power system. Since, the Voltage and current (limit to 1.5-2 pu) signals are modified during fault condition due to the control scheme applied in inverter of PV system which complies with the grid codes. So, the conventional power system protection schemes fails to operate correctly for such aforementioned condition. The current differential protection is employed in the protection system, which is immune to load encroachment and power swing. Also, It is simple to provide simultaneous tripping at both ends and multi phase auto reclosing due to its accuracy. In order to enhance sensitivity of current differential protection's under high resistance fault, the security is compromising. In order to improve both sensitivity and security of the relay, in this paper, a new protection methodology is proposed based on the DC transient current polarity. To test the effectiveness of the suggested technique,a 100 kW PV array connected to a 25 kV, 60 Hz grid system with a transmission line length of 25 km. Further, this system is simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC and MATLAB2018a. The simulation results are found correct and authentic hence, it is confirm that the proposed technique has ability to distinguish the internal and external faults.

articleTitle: Moth flame Optimisation based Allocation of DG and DSTATCOM in Radial Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Moth Flame Optimization (MFO) technique was introduced in this research to decide the size and location of D-STATCOM (DS) and distribution generation (DG) in a radial distribution system (RDS) under various scenarios. Loss minimization in the distribution network (DN) is a primary concern nowadays to improve voltage profile with a reduction in voltage deviation to maintain it within the acceptable limit as per IEEE standard 1547 and the reduction of line losses. Reactive power is compensated using DS & active power is compensated with the help of DG. Improvement of voltage profile, decrement in power loss, and energy-saving are made using optimal allocation (OA). MATLAB-2021a was used to obtain the IEEE 33 and 69 bus RDS simulation results.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Wavelet Transform-based Trans-multiplexer for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Satellite communication has become firmly estab-lished as one of three basic techniques for long-distance telecommunications. Multiplexing in satellite systems preserves channel resources and improves the temporal and computational complexity of the system. Filter bank-based multiplexing solutions are gaining popularity in the domain, as they achieve high data rates with relatively low error rates. Trans-multiplexers are applications of filter banks that convert time-division-multiplexed (TDM) signals to frequency-division-multiplexed (FDM) signals for transmission over a channel. Most trans-multiplexer systems use Fourier and Cosine transforms for filter design and signal reconstruction, which do not offer Perfect Reconstruction (PR) as the time domain information of the signal is discarded. This paper presents an algorithm that utilizes wavelet transform techniques for filter design to be used in trans-multiplexers. The work realizes the designed filters and trans-multiplexer system in MATLAB, and its performance is evaluated by testing with various channel models and mother wavelets. The simulated system outperforms a similar conventional system by a factor of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Speed Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Presence of communication network for transmission of signals in motors employed in electric/hybrid electric vehicles might lead to inefficient utilization of limited bandwidth, computational and energy resources. To overcome this issue, an event-triggering strategy is developed for control of permanent magnet synchronous motors in this paper. The control law of the motor is updated only when a predefined event-triggering condition is violated. This reduces the number the transmissions from sensor to the controller. Further, a field oriented PI-controller is designed for control of direct axis current, quadrature current and speed of the motor. The proposed control strategy aims at reducing the wear and tear of the motor while efficiently utilizing the resources and maintaining the system stability. The results proposed in the paper are compared with the sampled-data strategy.

articleTitle: Ensemble-based Load Forecasting for Smart Metered System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper discusses a new ensemble load forecasting technique to forecast the load at diverse nodes of a residential academic institute using smart metered data. The difficulties of establishing a precise load forecasting model is due to the complexity of electrical load in any distribution system. The accuracy of individual load forecasting methods is limited by the large load variations due to many factors like weather, time, day, season, etc. Hence, ensemble methods are developed to improve load forecasting performance. Two types of ensemble techniques including weighted average ensemble and stacking ensemble are developed and the load forecasting performance is compared. The proposed ensemble approach uses classical forecaster, the exponential smoothening (ES) method, and machine learning forecasters like support vector regression (SVR), feed-forward neural network (FFNN), and cascade forward neural network (CFNN) in different stages. The experimental result shows that the proposed stacking ensemble model provides precise and consistent performance of forecasting for smart meter-connected systems.

articleTitle: Achieving Cost Benefit Using Fuzzy Logic Based Charging Schemes for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The zero carbon emission target set by different countries in Confrence of Parties (COP 2021) has ignited the Electric Vehicle (EV) market all over the world. Increase in number of shares of EV in market influx more demand of electricity which will lead to more consumption and power distributors will use smart tariff strategy for there charging system. Hence, this paper proposes the charging scheme of EV based on fuzzy logic which will suggest the appropriate EV charger depending upon vehicle parameters via initial SoC, arrival time, departure time and the distance to be further travel. The performance of this fuzzy inference system is evaluated with respect to charging cost and peak load which results in prudential EVs charging without overloading power grid.

articleTitle: Single Phase 17-Level Asymmetric CHB Multilevel Inverter Using Fundamental Switching Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, a 17-level asymmetric Cascaded H-Bridge (CHB) converter with integrating a Level Doubling Circuit (LDC) is presented. A fundamental switching frequency modulation technique is adapted for the generation of required gate pulse to the proposed topology. The suggested architecture necessitates the use of two asymmetric DC sources with a 1:3 magnitude ratio, ten switches, and a self-balanced capacitor. By cascading the H Bridges, the suggested architecture can create a greater number of voltage levels. The proposed Asymmetric CHB inverter generates N levels with the help of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$log_{3}(\frac{\mathrm{N}+1}{2})$</tex> DC sources, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2+4 log_{3}(\frac{\mathrm{N}+1}{2})$</tex> switches, and a capacitor. In comparison to the existing topologies presented in literature, the proposed Asymmetric CHB requires fewer switches and DC sources for an N number of voltage levels. The proposed topology is simulated in the MATLAB/SIMULINK. A Level Shift - PWM (LS-PWM) method is implemented by considering the carrier frequency is equal to 50Hz. Further, the simulation results are verified experimentally using dSPACE 1104 by use of a prototype model made in a laboratory. In the output voltage waveform, the Total Hormonic Distortion (THD) is less than 5%.

articleTitle: Detection of Tannic Acid using Nd2O3 Modified Graphite Electrode
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Tannic acid is widely found in fruits, tea samples and other beverages. It is also used as a preservative to increase the shelf life of meat and fish fillets. In this work, simple and affordable neodymium (III) oxide nanoparticles embedded carbon electrode (Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> @GP) has been developed for the detection of tannic acid. A three electrode setup has been used to assess the performance of the Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> @GP electrode using cyclic voltammetry (CV). The cyclic voltammetry (CV) responses reveal that the developed electrode is successfully able to trace the presence of tannic acid. The linear working range of the electrode is found to be 5 to 200µM. The limit of detection (LOD) was found to be 0.7µM. This electrochemical procedure can thus be used in the detection of tannic acid in various food and beverages consumed in our daily life.

articleTitle: TCAD Analysis of Dielectric Pocket Nanowire Junctionless Field-Effect Transistor based Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)

authors.preferredName: Vanjarapu N M S R Narendra

abstract: In this article, the neutral biomolecules with different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-values using label free detection with potential capability of Dielectric Pocket Nanowire Junctionless Field-effect Transistor (DP-NWJLFET) based biosensor is explored. 3D TCAD simulation of the proposed device is investigated by varying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-value (from 1 to 10) of the target biomolecules to be detected in the cavity region formed at source end. To study the performance of the proposed biosensor, various performance parameters like drain current, threshold voltage and center potential are analyzed for different neutral biomolecules. It is observed that off-state current decreases with increasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k- \text{value}$</tex> of the biomolecules and attains its lowest value for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k=10$</tex>, thus showing a higher sensitivity for the same biomolecules i.e. Keratin. Furthermore, shift in the threshold voltage is also found to be maximum i.e. 0.218 when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k-\text{value}$</tex> of the biomolecules is varied for 1 to 10. The impact of various biomolecules on the central potential is also demonstrated in this work and found to be increasing with increasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k-\text{value}$</tex> of the biomolecules in the cavity, which further caused a reduction in the off-state current of the proposed device.

articleTitle: Dielectric Engineered Cylindrical Junctionless FET for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper we have analyzed the impact of high-k dielectric as gate oxide on the junctionless field-effect transistor (JLFET). Four different dielectric materials as gate oxide have been considered and analyzed in this work. The gate oxide thickness is taken as 1 nm. It has been observed on utilizing the high-k material as a dielectric constant, the leakage of the device is reduced while there is no significant change in the ON-state current. 3D Silvaco ATLAS simulator has been used to perform the simulations for this work.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of Various C-Rate Type of BESS for Radial Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Peak demand is the most significant factor for the load operating cost determination. Due to heavy burden on national grids at peak hours of day time, the DISCOM utilities get charged heavily according to heavy peak load demand, during peak hours of a day. In this paper optimal BESS placement and sizing is done by Teacher Learner Based Optimization (TLBO), to reduce the hourly peak load variation burden on grid during peak hours. Six different C-Rate types of batteries i.e., 0.5C, 0.08C, 0.25C, 0.33C, 0.167C and 1C have been examined for voltage profile improvement during peak hours without any significant increment in power loss. With the optimal located and sized BESS in distribution side of grid will leads to have a reliable with efficient grid support and reduced power loss help to grid load power demand diversification. In this paper Reliability test system model is used for the reliability analysis per hour for radial IEEE 33 bus distribution networks, and results are verified and simulated in MATLAB 2019b software.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Multi-Agent Non-identical Chaotic Systems through Model Matching Control using Feedback Linearization
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, a nonlinear Model Matching control problem is presented based on feedback linearization technique. For the analysis purpose, the output synchronization case is considered. The proposed synchronization methodology utilizes a control law acquired from graph theory and takes care of the model-matching control for multi-agent systems. Especially, set of non-identical chaotic systems are considered as Plant and Model, combination where the relative degree of the systems is less than the order of the system. The asymptotic convergence error dynamics is proved using the Routh-Hurwitz method. The effectiveness of the proposed procedure is verified using MATLAB simulations. For example, the 3D Lorenz chaotic system and 4D Lüchaotic system are considered to achieve synchronization in multi-agent systems configuration.

articleTitle: An assessment of Metanil Yellow Adulteration in Pigeon Pea using NIR Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this work, NIR (Near infrared) spectroscopy is used to assess metanil yellow adulteration present in pigeon pea. The NIR data for both raw and adulterated samples was analyzed. Transmission mode NIR spectrometer measurements were performed within the wavelength range of 900–1700 nm. In order to analyze spectral data, chemometrics was applied. A principal component analysis (PCA) was used to analyze and distinguish six different sample. The PCA plot showed that six samples clustered together effectively. NIR data obtained in this study had a very high-class separability index measuring 88.29. Partial least square regression (PLSR) analysis and principal component regression (PCR) were used to predict and correlate metanil yellow levels in this study. An average prediction accuracy of 99.995 and 99.997% were provided by the prediction algorithms, with a correlation factor of 0.85 and 0.92 respectively. The results of the primary evaluation strongly suggest that NIR spectroscopy may be employed to assess traces of meta nil yellow adulteration in pigeon pea samples.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Motors with Intelligent Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Permanent magnet brushless dc (PMBLDC) motors are reported to be having good performance as compared to induction motors and others conventional motors. Therefore PMBLDC motors have viable option with a cost effective solution with high performance. Conventional control of PMBLDC motors is not able to have full benefits out of these motors. The control with intelligence is reported to have more enhanced performance and good results. Fuzzy logic is supposed to have inbuilt intelligence and also fuzzy logic based controllers are most popular in process control and some industrial application. This paper therefore will target upon the use of Fuzzy logic based controller to tap the maximum benefits out of PMBLDC motors. Simulation of PMBLDC motor with the PID controller and Fuzzy logic based controller is done in MATLAB simulation environment. The comparison between different parameters i.e. speed, torque and currents with different types of controllers is also reported.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in DC Microgrid Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A complex protection challenge has hampered the widespread acceptance of DC microgrids despite their numerous advantages, including increased efficiency and stability, as well as the ease with which they can be integrated with renewable energy sources (RES). With the lack of natural zero crossing, intermittent nature of RES, as well as the high likelihood of distributed energy resource (DER) outages, make the task of fault detection and classification even more difficult. A DC microgrid protection strategy is proposed in this paper that is more resilient to weather uncertainty and probable generation outages. In order detect and classify the fault, a convolution neural network (CNN) based technique is used in this paper. The proposed scheme minimizes the complexity and cost associated with the feature extraction process. The CNN classifier correctly differentiates between all events, and its performance is demonstrated by a variety of metrics. MATLAB/Simulink platform is used to model the DC microgrid system.

articleTitle: Event - Triggered Control of Distributed Networked Control Systems with Time-varying Coupling Strength
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Control of interconnected system communicating over limited network resources and having limited energy is a challenging task. With this objective, an event-triggering strategy for control of nonlinear distributed networked systems with time-varying coupling strength has been proposed in this paper. In the proposed methodology, the nonlinear subsystems are modelled through Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy approximation technique and the event-triggered controller is developed using parallel distributed compensation. A state based event-triggering strategy is proposed wherein each subsystem transmits its information over a network only when its local error exceeds a predetermined threshold value. This paper addresses the co-design problem of triggering parameters and feedback controller gain of nonlinear distributed networked systems with time-varying coupling strength. The efficacy of the results is validated via a simulation example.

articleTitle: A review of Delineation, Burgeoning and Performance of Solar Energy for Drying Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Using Solar energy to dry is one of the old techniques which is rehearsed still today. In prior days, sunlight-based energy was utilized for the conservation of food, garments, and construction materials, drying of soil breaks and so forth, however, all things considered, there were chances of harm by bugs, dust, downpour, soil and a lot more things. Thusly, to kill these issues, various kinds of sun-oriented dryers became an integral factor. The antiquated strategy was an open drying framework which went with many hustles. Thus, to further develop this sun based dryers are depicted and determined their boundaries to acquire a quicker working, more adequacy and to advance better cleanliness and nature of items. Present-day sunlight-based drying techniques are utilized for safeguarding the farming items, drying natural products, drying floor coverings, drying blocks, and drying harvests. In this paper, various techniques for sunlight-based drying have been concentrated alongside their depiction.

articleTitle: Investigation of Pairwise Error Probability of α-µ Fading Channel in Spatially modulated MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper comprises of pairwise error probability analysis of SM-MIMO employing α - µ fading channel considering M-PSK modulation scheme. Analysis has been done for different values of α and µ. The investigation has also done for 2-PSK, 4-PSK and 8-PSK techniques of α - µ fading channel by changing number of transmitting antennas and receiving antennas. The comparison has been done on the basis of changing parameters as the simulation results. It can also be seen from the analytical result and simulation result, as the modulation increase the performance of the system degraded.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Line Parameters using Synchrophasors Incorporated with Kalman Filter for Dynamic Loading
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Transmission line parameters is one of the most important aspects of the power system as it defines the safety, control and operation of the power system. This paper describes the use of PMUs data for the measurement of transmission line parameters. Earlier this data is obtained theoretically which doesn't support the real condition due to variation of line parameters due to environmental condition. The equivalent pi-model of medium transmission line is used for analysis. The measurement obtained to PMUs also contains some random error or uncertainty. This error is introduced while taking reading from CTs or PTs. This error must be filtered there are various filter which can be used for filtering the input, here Kalman filter is choose as due to its advantage of fast and reliable results. Kalman filter is used to filter out this error to get the estimated output near to the true value. This system is then tested for three cases of varying load conditions. Firstly, it is tested out for normal load then higher active power load i.e step load and then it is tested with ramp load. The results came out be almost in line with true value with minimalistic error.

articleTitle: Digital Simulation of a 60-Pulse GTO-Based Voltage Source Converter in a Unified Power Flow Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The unified power flow controller (UPFC) is a series and shunt compensatory voltage source converter (VSC) based on the flexible ac transmission technology (FACT). The FACT device can be linked to a transmission line in a variety of ways, including series and shunt combinations in multiline transmission systems. On an electric transmission line, UPFC is utilized for reactive power correction. A static synchronous compensation device is an imbalanced current electricity network regulating device. The digital simulation of the shunt voltage source converter operates as STATCOM controlling the voltage at the bus and series converter. In this paper, MATLAB/Simulink is used to control the series and shunt converters of a UPFC transmission line. It is premised on power electronics voltage source converter with 48-pulse VSC and 60-pulse VSC, the performance of the UPFC scheme connected to the 500kv transmission line. The simulation results for 60-, 48-pulse gate turn-off (GTO) based VSC 100MVAR UPFC coupled to two ac bus power systems are shown as simulation results. The VSC currents and supplies require reactive power in single-line to ground (L-G) and line-to-line (L-L) faults and three-phase system failures.

articleTitle: Design of a High Performance PMSM for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The design of a high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor has been discussed in this work with the help of Ansys Maxwell. The study proposes a 110kW radial PMSM with a maximum rotational speed of 13300 rpm. The developed motor can reach a efficiency of over 96 percent thanks to the high speed. Electrical and mechanical design are both challenged by the high speed.

articleTitle: A Current-Mode Active Filter using VDCCs and Only Grounded Passive Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A new second-order active filter is designed with the help of an active building block i.e. Voltage Differencing Current Conveyor (VDCC). The proposed network of a universal filter utilizes only two VDCCs and three grounded passive elements. The presented current mode active filter can generate all required responses, such as band pass, low pass, and high pass, from its high impedance port when input is fed into the low impedance port, resulting in a completely fully cascadable filter. The proposed circuit practicality is demonstrated through mathematical analysis such as ideal, non-ideal, sensitivity, and parasitics analysis. The simulation results are further confirmed using Cadence OrCAD PSPICE software, which includes 0.18µm CMOS technology parameters that match the theory.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Compact Triple band Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents a Compact Triple band Mi-crostrip patch antenna by using Shorting post and Gap coupled Method for C, X, Ku band application. In this design for feeding Coaxial probe technique is used which is given to central patch only which is made for X band application. Rogers RT6010LM lossy material is used as a substrate with a dielectric constant of 10.7 and having thickness of 1.6 mm. This substrate with high dielectric constant is used to make compact overall size of the proposed antenna. For further reduction of the proposed antenna and to improve the working efficiency of it, Shorting post(shorting bar) method is used. Gap coupled method is analyzed to resonate it at three different frequencies. This compactness and triple band property of the proposed antenna makes it suitable for medical, Radar, Satellite application. The proposed antenna represents triple band(C/X/Ku) triple band antenna that mainly covers 6.3 GHZ for Wireless application STM Link 1 (Synchronous Transport Module Level-1), 9.4 GHz satisfies the application for Radio Detection and Ranging(RADAR) application and 14.3 GHz is applicable for Satellite application. The simulation process has been done using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Studio Software. For proper impedance matching the outer and inner radius of the probe is taken 0.9mm and 0.3mm Respectively. The properties of antenna such as Return loss, Directivity, Gain etc are determined.

articleTitle: Extreme Learning Machine Based Transient Stability Assessment: An Energy Function Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: One of the most challenging task at Energy Control Centre is the prediction of transient stability. Deregulation and ever increasing integration of renewables has made it complex and more demanding in terms of frequent evaluations. Transient Stability Assessment is computationally intensive task and longer computation cycle brings in obsolete results as system operating state evolves continuously. Extreme learning machine (ELM) offers prediction results comparable to other state-of-art learning methods and has much quicker learning curve. WSCC 3-machine 9-bus system and IEEE 39-bus New England test power system are considered to demonstrate the superiority of ELM as a predictive model. ELM is trained using data points generated through transient energy function (TEF) approach. Transient energy terms along with real and reactive power and fault location are used as input attributes for ELM to quickly and accurately determine transient stability margin (TEM).

articleTitle: Detection of Andrographolide Using Platinum Electrode Based Electrochemical System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this work, a sensitive electrochemical sensor system for the detection of Andrographolide molecule has been studied using the noble metal platinum (Pt) based working electrode. A three-electrode configuration was used to examine and analyze the electrochemical response of the Pt working electrode along with a reference electrode based on silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) and a steel based counter electrode. Experimental studies were performed using electrochemical measurement techniques such as cyclic voltammetry (CV) and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV). A satisfactory linear range of electrochemical responses were obtained for several concentrations of andrographolide molecule in the linear range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\ \mu \mathrm{M}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\ \mu \mathrm{M}$</tex> with a limit of detection (LOD) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.68\ \mu \mathrm{M}$</tex>. The linear enhancement of oxidation maximum currents was also investigated using the differential pulse voltammetry technique with the linear rise in the scan rate. The Pt electrode was applied over real Andrographis paniculate samples i.e., kalmegh leaf extracts as well for real sample analysis and revealed satisfactory recovery rates of 103% and 102.2% respectively. Thus, this simple electrochemical sensing technique of andrographolide detection may be used extensively for consuming kalmegh in our daily life for various herbal medicinal applications.

articleTitle: Static PEMFC Model Simulation to Exhibit the Working with Converter
